## Testing on a low-spec PC (load test)

`reascratch_load_test.lua` checks whether ReaScratch runs comfortably on this PC.

1. With the audio settings you normally use (ASIO and so on, and the same buffer size as for the show), open a project with imported videos, open the video window and keep the video sync running (without it, the result says no video load was included). In a project with deck B, import into deck B too (the test does not start while a deck is empty).
2. Run `reascratch_load_test.lua` from the action list (after running setup, searching for "`reascratch`" finds it; if not, load it with `New action...` > `Load ReaScript...`).
3. You are asked “Start the load test (about 40 s)?”: “Yes: with sound (turn the volume down first)”, “No: measure muted”, “Cancel: do not start”.
4. It takes about 40 seconds (the first 10 seconds with things as they are, then each deck scratches automatically for 30 seconds and reloads a sample once along the way). Do not touch the mouse or keyboard meanwhile. To stop early, run it again.
5. When it finishes, the results are shown and saved to `ReaScratch_load_test_<date>_<time>.txt` in the REAPER resource folder.

Reading the results:

- **Dropouts**: the number of times audio processing fell behind, counted by ReaScratch itself (REAPER's own counter is shown too, but it has been found to miss some even with ASIO, so go by ReaScratch's count). Even one during the automatic scratching means the sound may drop out during a show as it is. Make the video height smaller in setup (540 or 360) or the audio buffer larger, and test again. With WaveOut or DirectSound, dropouts caused by tracks or plug-ins other than ReaScratch may not be counted.
- **JSFX load**: the share of each processing time slot that ReaScratch used. If the "heaviest moments" of all decks add up to more than 70%, there is little headroom left when other work (such as video) piles on.
- **Screen updates**: the longest time the screen drawing and the video following stalled. Above 0.25 s, the picture may look like it hitches.
